item.title: Former U.S. army soldier recounts Gaza experience in campus talk
item.description: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) whistleblower Anthony Aguilar shared firsthand accounts of conditions at Gaza aid sites, describing war crimes and U.S. complicity. The post Former U.S. army soldier recounts Gaza experience in campus talk appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Former Stanford professor Stephen Kosslyn Ph.D. ’74 denies sexual assault claim
item.description: Kosslyn shared a statement responding to The Daily’s reporting on a disputed sexual assault claim against him by one of Jeffrey Epstein’s victims. The post Former Stanford professor Stephen Kosslyn Ph.D. ’74 denies sexual assault claim appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: From the Community | This Ash Wednesday, choose compassion over optimization
item.description: Ariana Duduna '28 reflects on Ash Wednesday, claiming it is a way for Catholics and non-Catholics alike to reflect on their mortality and join in community rather than focus on their own self advancement. The post From the Community | This Ash Wednesday, choose compassion over optimization appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Dirty Hungry Homosexuals: ‘Paradise Rot’ probes the sensuality of sound
item.description: Not everything that eats you has to do so using its mouth. In Jenny Hval’s novel, Jo rapidly becomes consumed by thoughts of her roommate Carral, accentuating the blurring nature of queer desire. The post Dirty Hungry Homosexuals: ‘Paradise Rot’ probes the sensuality of sound appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Choose Your Own Adventure: A GSB student reflects on TreeHacks 2026
item.description: TreeHacks embodies a culture of exploration and creativity over ruthless efficiency, writes Jain. The post Choose Your Own Adventure: A GSB student reflects on TreeHacks 2026 appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Irony as armor: Yale’s Maurice Samuels explores literary survival in the ‘gray zone’ of tyranny
item.description: Using 19th-century France as a parallel to modern democratic erosion, the Yale historian argued that Charles Baudelaire’s "gray zone" of complicity and irony, rather than heroic exile, represents the most typical experience of a writer surviving under tyranny. The post Irony as armor: Yale’s Maurice Samuels explores literary survival in the ‘gray zone’ of tyranny appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Stanford wrestling upsets No. 12 Pitt
item.description: No. 23 Stanford shocked No. 12 Pittsburgh at Maples on Sunday, sweeping the first six bouts to secure a statement victory behind strong ranked performances. The post Stanford wrestling upsets No. 12 Pitt appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Collective climate action is driven by positive messaging, Stanford research finds
item.description: Stanford researchers investigated which types of climate messaging are most effective in motivating people to take collective action, finding that focusing on past successes ranks the highest. The post Collective climate action is driven by positive messaging, Stanford research finds appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.description: The internship grind is known far and wide. Asian Auntie addresses our reader and gives them some much needed advice. She certainly knows a thing or two. The post Ask Your Asian Auntie: Internship applications are the worst! appeared first on The Stanford Daily.
